headline: CORRECTION + update: AVN's H1/Q2 FY26 results were actually published Aug 28 (missed that review) — 'Sep 2 earnings' was a stale bad date. Pulled the real PSX filing: consolidated H1 swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M net loss (EPS −0.62 vs +0.38) despite +34% revenue growth, driven by a 45% jump in admin/selling costs and a collapse in the one-off 'other income' that flattered last year. No dividend declared. This is hard confirmation of the margin-collapse thesis, not new event risk to wait through — EXIT call reinforced, still unexecuted (24,500 shares unchanged). Separately: Portfolio value ~Rs 10.27M, P/L +Rs 223K (+2.22% on cost), down from +2.55% three days ago on a broad market pullback (KSE-100 −0.41% to 176,975.67 on Middle East/US-Iran tension), not AVN-specific — AVN itself actually rose 2.98% to Rs 30.05 today. No other holding moved >5% or had material fresh news.

Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) widened slightly to ~6.6% (from ~6.3% Friday) — still short of the 10% line that would justify deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve, but worth watching if Middle East tension escalates further. Backdrop otherwise unchanged: SBP holding at 11.5% since the Jul 27 pause, $1.3B IMF EFF/RSF tranche already reflected, inflation easing toward the 5-7% target band — no new SBP or IMF news this review. AVN — CORRECTION: 'Sep 2 earnings' was a stale third-party estimate; the real H1/Q2 FY26 results were published Aug 28 and were missed that review. Pulled the actual PSX filing today: consolidated H1 revenue +34% YoY (Rs 7.04B) but net result swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M loss (EPS −0.62 vs +0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M (EPS −0.74) from a Rs 104M loss a year earlier; standalone same pattern (H1 +Rs 136M profit → −Rs 66M loss). No dividend declared. Driver: admin/selling expenses +45% YoY outpacing revenue growth, and 'other income' that cushioned last year's profit (Rs 162M in H1 2025) fell to Rs 77M this year. This is confirmed board-level deterioration, harder evidence than what was on file before. The stock itself rose to Rs 30.05 today (+2.98% from Friday's Rs 29.18) but that's a bounce, not a reversal — remains −33.3% on cost. The Aug 25 EXIT call is now unexecuted through 4 reviews with the full 24,500 shares still in holdings; there is no earnings catalyst left to wait for before Q3. EFERT — no news beyond what's already on file (H1 revenue −12%, profit −16% YoY, Rs 3.75/share H1 dividends paid, urea glut with management holding the Rs 150/bag premium, banking on H2 seasonal demand); stays on WATCH into Q3. FABL — checked again, still no published ex-date for the Aug 6 Rs 1.50/share interim. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally this session (last commit 10:37 PKT) — no repeat of Friday's feed outage. Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 18 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue is still unresolved and needs a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — H1 report confirms swing to a real net loss; EXIT call now backed by hard numbers, still unexecuted
actions.detail: CORRECTION: the 'Sep 2 earnings' date tracked in prior reviews was wrong (a stale third-party estimate) — the actual H1/Q2 FY26 results were published Aug 28 (board meeting that day) and were missed in that review. Pulled directly from the PSX filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew a healthy +34% YoY (Rs 7.04B) but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS −Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M (EPS −Rs 0.74) from a Rs 104M loss a year earlier. Standalone tells the same story (H1 swung from +Rs 136M profit to −Rs 66M loss). No dividend declared (NIL). Cause: admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY, far outpacing revenue growth, plus 'other income' that cushioned last year's profit (Rs 162M in H1 2025) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics. This is real, board-confirmed deterioration — not a rumor or a single bad line item — and it confirms the margin-collapse thesis with harder numbers than previously on file. Now −33.3% on cost (Rs 30.05). No further earnings catalyst is pending before Q3; there is no reason left to keep waiting. Recommend selling the entire position at market now.

actions.title: Fatima Fertilizer — H1 results beat (profit +20.7%), but skipped the interim dividend
actions.detail: +46.3% (Rs 157.25, down slightly since last review despite the earnings beat — the dividend skip likely weighed more than the profit growth did). But the board chose not to declare an interim dividend, citing an uncertain operating environment, geopolitical risk, and unresolved GIDC exposure; management was explicit this isn't a policy change. Earnings thesis confirmed, moving off WATCH back to HOLD, but worth checking the next dividend announcement to see if the skip was a one-off or the start of a pattern.
